Sharanjith Shetty K., Advocate) This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227 Of The Constituttion Of India Praying To Quash The Order Dtd 23/03/2023 Passed By The R-2 In Appeal No. 7/2022-23 Vide Annexure-K In Confirming The Order Of Rejecting The Application Of The Petitioner For Grant Of Trade License Under The Endorsement Dtd 29/09/2022 Vide Annexure-H And Grant Trade License To The Petitioner As Sought Under The Application Dtd 19/09/2022 Vide Annexure-G. This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing In 'B' Group This Day, The Court Made The Following: Order
texts.facts: 1. The petitioner-company is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs: a) Issue of writ or order in the nature of certiorari and quash the order dtd 23/03/2023 passed by the R-2 in appeal No.7/2022-23 vide Annexure-K in confirming the order of rejecting the application of the petitioner for grant of trade license under the endorsement dtd 29/09/2022 vide Annexure-H and grant trade license to the petitioner as sought under the application dtd 19/09/2022 vide Annexure-G. b) Pass such other or further orders as this Hon'ble authority may deems fit to pass in NC: 2023:KHC:33059 the circumstances of the case and in the interests of justice and equity. Hasan Ashok Trading Pvt. Ltd vs The Panchayath Development Officer on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106555342/ 2 2. The petitioner is a company incorporated under the provisions of the Companies Act, 1956 registered with the Registrar of Companies with an object of dealing with food articles and has received necessary permission and licences from the Food Safety and Standards Authority under the Food and Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ['FSS Act' for short]. The petitioner in order to conduct retail business dealing with meat including beef had entered into a lease agreement in respect of a shop premises located in Mysore-Mangaluru Highway under the hope that licence will be granted by respondent No.1 for carrying out said business. 3. The petitioner made an application for trade licence for the said business enclosing 'No objection' letters from the neighbours. However, the said application came to be rejected by respondents on the ground that the location of the retail outlet is close to a school and old age home and members of the of the general public are objecting to it. NC: 2023:KHC:33059 4. The petitioner challenged the endorsement dated 29.09.2022 in Appeal No.7/2022-23 which again came to be dismissed and it is in that background that the petitioner is before this court seeking for the aforesaid reliefs.
texts.arguments: 5. The contention of Sri.Aravind Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner is that once the neighbours have issued 'No objection' letters and the Food Safety and Standards Authority has issued necessary licences, the respondents cannot deny the issuance of trade licence to the petitioner muchless on the ground communicated in the impugned endorsement. He submits that there is no business which is carried on by the petitioner which is offensive or dangerous, the business being only for vending of meat as an eatery, there is no slaughterhouse activity that would be carried out, no live animals will be kept at the location and as such, the respondents ought to have granted the trade licence. 6. Sri.Sharanjith Shetty, learned counsel for respondents, however, submits that there are certain objections received from general public and that since the eatery is NC: 2023:KHC:33059 located near a school and an old age home, the trade licence has been refused. In this regard, he relies upon Section 68 of the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 ['Act' for short] to contend that there is power vested with the Authority to reject the licence sought for in terms thereto. No place within the jurisdiction of a Grama Panchayat shall be used as a hotel, restaurant, eating house, coffee-house, sweetmeat shop, bakery, Hasan Ashok Trading Pvt. Ltd vs The Panchayath Development Officer on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106555342/ 3 boarding house or lodging house (other than a hostel recognised by the Government), or a dharmashala or for manufacturing ice or aerated water except under a licence granted or renewed by the Grama Panchayat and except in accordance with conditions specified therein. The said provision does not confer any right or authority on part of respondent-Panchayat to reject an application for running a hotel, eatery, etc. on account of objections by general public or the same being close to a school or old age home. 10. The provisions contained under Section 68 cannot said to be a prohibition inasmuch as the provision relates to control of a hotel, eatery, lodging house, etc.
